subtopics.content: a. Definition of Agriculture
subtopics.objective: Use the definition of Agriculture in modern terms as it relates to production, processing and marketing.

subtopics.content: b. Branches of Agriculture
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between the various branches of Agriculture.

subtopics.content: c. Types of Agriculture, i.e. subsistence and commercial
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between the various types of Agriculture, their advantages and disadvantages and their respective problems.

subtopics.content: i. Provision of raw materials for agro-allied industries
subtopics.objective: Relate agricultural benefits to individual farmers and relate agro-allied industries to their respective raw materials.

subtopics.content: ii. Provision of employment
subtopics.objective: Relate the various contributions of Agriculture to economic development in West Africa.

subtopics.content: iii. Development of rural areas, etc.
subtopics.objective: Relate the various contributions of Agriculture to economic development in West Africa.

subtopics.content: a. Ecological zones of West Africa
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between the features of the ecological zones in West Africa.

subtopics.content: b. Agricultural products of each ecological zone
subtopics.objective: Classify agricultural products according to each ecological zone.

subtopics.content: c. Environmental factors and their effects on crop and livestock production
subtopics.objective: Differentiate abiotic from biotic factors affecting agricultural production.

subtopics.content: a. First and second laws of Mendel
subtopics.objective: Apply the first and second laws of Mendel to genetics.

subtopics.content: b. Cell division
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between the types of cell division.

subtopics.content: c. Terminologies, e.g. locus, alleles, genotype, dominance
subtopics.objective: Determine the outcome of genetic crossing involving homozygous and heterozygous traits, and compute simple probability ratios.

subtopics.content: d. Methods of crop improvement, e.g. introduction, selection, crossing, quarantine, etc.
subtopics.objective: Give reasons for crop improvement; distinguish between methods of crop improvement and their respective advantages and disadvantages.

subtopics.content: e. Methods of animal improvement, e.g. introduction, breeding, quarantine and selection; breeding systems—inbreeding, line-breeding, crossbreeding, artificial insemination
subtopics.objective: Give reasons for animal improvement; differentiate between methods of animal improvement and their respective advantages and disadvantages.

subtopics.content: Examples of farm inputs, e.g. planting materials, agrochemicals, etc.
subtopics.objective: Classify different types of farm inputs and their uses.

topics.title: History of Agricultural Development in West Africa

subtopics.content: a. Agricultural systems, e.g. shifting cultivation, bush fallowing, etc.
subtopics.objective: Compare various agricultural systems.

subtopics.content: b. Problems of agricultural development, e.g. land tenure systems, inadequate infrastructure, inadequate finance for agriculture, environmental degradation, etc.
subtopics.objective: Identify problems of agricultural development, their effects and propose solutions.

subtopics.content: c. Establishment of national research institutes, e.g. NCRI, IAR, IAR&T, CRIN, NIFOR, FRIN, RRI, NRCRI, NIHORT, LCRI, and international research institutes, e.g. IITA, ILRI, ICRISAT, WARDA, leading to increased application of science to agricultural development
subtopics.objective: Trace the history of research institutes from past to present and assess their role in agricultural development.

subtopics.content: d. Agricultural Development Projects (ADPs), e.g. RTEP, FADAMA, etc.
subtopics.objective: Give reasons for the establishment of ADPs.

subtopics.content: e. National agricultural programmes, such as OFN, NAFPP, NALDA, Green Revolution, NCRPs, NARP, Project Coordinating Unit (PCU), etc.
subtopics.objective: Evaluate the contributions of national agricultural programmes.

topics.title: Roles of Government and NGOs in Agricultural Development

subtopics.content: a. Development of fiscal policies favourable to agricultural production, e.g. import duties and bans on importation
subtopics.objective: Evaluate the effects of government policies on agricultural development.

subtopics.content: b. Agricultural laws and reforms, e.g. Land Use Act
subtopics.objective: Identify agricultural laws and their effect on agricultural production.

subtopics.content: c. Government programmes aimed at agricultural development, e.g. subsidies and credit facilities
subtopics.objective: Identify the various agricultural incentives provided by government and assess their effects on agricultural development.

subtopics.content: d. Provision of infrastructure, e.g. transport and communication systems
subtopics.objective: Compare the various infrastructural facilities provided by government and their uses.

subtopics.content: e. Contribution of NGOs to agricultural development
subtopics.objective: Examine the roles of NGOs in the development of agriculture.

subtopics.content: a. Rock formation
subtopics.objective: Identify the major types of rocks and their formation.

subtopics.content: b. Factors affecting rock weathering and soil formation
subtopics.objective: Identify major types and properties of soils, and the factors and processes of soil formation.

subtopics.content: c. Physical properties of soil: soil profile; soil components, texture and structure
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between the horizons in a soil profile; differentiate between soil components; compute the proportion of soil components; analyse soil into its component parts; determine the water-holding capacity of soil.

subtopics.content: d. Chemical properties of soil: soil acidity and alkalinity; chemical components of soil, e.g. silicate
subtopics.objective: Determine the soil pH.

subtopics.content: a. Soil water: importance, sources, movement, management and conservation
subtopics.objective: Compare capillary, gravitational and hygroscopic water; determine water-holding capacity, wilting points, and plant-available and unavailable water; identify methods of soil-water management and conservation.

subtopics.content: b. Soil conservation: meaning and importance; causes, effects, prevention and control of leaching, erosion, continuous cropping, burning and oxidation of organic matter
subtopics.objective: Identify the causes of erosion and leaching and determine control methods.

subtopics.content: c. Irrigation and drainage methods
subtopics.objective: Classify irrigation and drainage systems; examine their importance and challenges.

subtopics.content: a. Macro- and micronutrients and their roles in plant nutrition; carbon, water and nitrogen cycles
subtopics.objective: Classify plant nutrients and identify factors affecting their availability.

subtopics.content: b. The living population of the soil (flora and fauna) and their roles in soil fertility
subtopics.objective: Examine the roles of soil flora and fauna in maintaining soil fertility.

subtopics.content: c. Maintenance of soil fertility: methods such as cover crops and application of organic manures
subtopics.objective: Compare methods of maintaining soil fertility; differentiate between organic and inorganic fertilizer and their methods of application; determine common fertilizer ratios.

subtopics.content: d. Nutrient deficiency symptoms, e.g. chlorosis, sickle leaves, stunting and apical necrosis
subtopics.objective: Identify deficiency symptoms and their causes, and suggest remedies.

subtopics.content: a. Principles and practices of land preparation and soil tillage
subtopics.objective: Compare methods of land preparation and soil tillage in relation to different groups of crops, including their advantages and disadvantages.

subtopics.content: b. Factors affecting choice of tillage methods: zero tillage, minimum tillage, etc.
subtopics.objective: Give reasons for the choice of tillage methods.

subtopics.content: a. Parts of monocot and dicot crop plants and their functions
subtopics.objective: Identify crop plant parts and their functions; distinguish between monocot and dicot crop plants.

subtopics.content: b. Anatomy and morphology of storage organs of common crop plants
subtopics.objective: Identify various storage organs of crop plants.

subtopics.content: a. Gametogenesis
subtopics.objective: Examine the process of gamete formation.

subtopics.content: b. Pollination
subtopics.objective: Identify the different types of pollination.

subtopics.content: c. Fertilization
subtopics.objective: Analyse the process of fertilization.

subtopics.content: d. Embryo formation and development
subtopics.objective: Trace embryo formation and development to the formation of seeds and fruits.

subtopics.content: a. Sexual propagation: use of seeds, seed viability, viability test, seed rate and seed germination
subtopics.objective: Classify crops propagated by sexual methods; determine seed viability and seed rate; differentiate between types of seed germination; examine conditions for seed germination.

subtopics.content: b. Asexual (vegetative) propagation, e.g. cutting, budding, grafting and layering
subtopics.objective: Classify crops into different vegetative propagation methods.

subtopics.content: c. Nursery and nursery management
subtopics.objective: Determine appropriate nursery sites and types, including their advantages and disadvantages; apply techniques of transplanting seedlings.

topics.title: Cropping Systems, Planting Patterns and Plant Densities

subtopics.content: a. Cropping systems: monocropping, mixed, multiple, inter-, relay-, strip- and rotational cropping
subtopics.objective: Identify and compare cropping systems and apply different systems to solve agricultural problems.

subtopics.content: b. Planting patterns: broadcasting, row spacing and drilling
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between the various planting patterns.

subtopics.content: c. Plant densities: single, double and multiple stands
subtopics.objective: Examine types of plant densities and their effects on crop yield; compute plant density per hectare.

subtopics.content: General study of common and scientific names, gross morphology, anatomy of storage organs, propagation, husbandry, harvesting, processing, storage, diseases, pests and economic importance of crops
subtopics.objective: Apply propagation, husbandry, harvesting, processing and storage methods to each crop; identify common diseases and pests and their effects on yield; determine the economic importance of crops and relate it to national economic development.

subtopics.content: Group 1: Cereals, e.g. maize, guinea corn and rice
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of cereals.

subtopics.content: Group 2: Legumes, e.g. cowpea, groundnut and soybean
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of legumes.

subtopics.content: Group 3: Tubers, e.g. yam, cassava and sweet potatoes
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of tubers.

subtopics.content: Group 4: Vegetables and spices, e.g. tomatoes, eggplant, pepper, onions, okra, cabbage and Amaranthus species
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of vegetables and spices.

subtopics.content: Group 5: Fruits, e.g. citrus, pineapple and pawpaw
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of fruits.

subtopics.content: Group 6: Beverages, e.g. cocoa, kola and coffee
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of beverage crops.

subtopics.content: Group 7: Oils, e.g. oil palm, coconut and shea butter
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of oil crops.

subtopics.content: Group 8: Latex, e.g. para rubber and gum Arabic
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of latex crops.

subtopics.content: Group 9: Fibres, e.g. jute, cotton and sisal hemp
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of fibre crops.

subtopics.content: Group 10: Sugars, e.g. sugarcane and beet
subtopics.objective: Apply appropriate crop husbandry and identify the diseases, pests, uses and economic importance of sugar crops.

subtopics.content: a. Gross morphology, propagation and husbandry of common pasture grasses and legumes; establishment, maintenance, conservation and uses of pastures and forage crops
subtopics.objective: Classify common pasture grasses and legumes; differentiate pasture and forage crops by common and scientific names; distinguish methods of pasture conservation, e.g. hay- and silage-making.

subtopics.content: b. Natural grasslands and their distribution in West Africa
subtopics.objective: Relate vegetation zones to their dominant pasture species.

subtopics.content: c. Range management
subtopics.objective: Determine range types and utilization of range resources in Nigeria.

subtopics.content: Identification, establishment, maintenance and uses of ornamental trees, shrubs and flowers
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between common ornamental trees, shrubs and flowers; determine their uses and maintenance.

subtopics.content: a. Gross morphology, methods of reproduction and dispersal, and effects of weeds
subtopics.objective: Identify weeds by common and scientific names; classify weeds by mode of dispersal; identify characteristic features of weeds.

subtopics.content: b. Weed control methods: weeding, mulching, cover cropping, tillage, herbicides and trap cropping
subtopics.objective: Apply various weed-control methods.

subtopics.content: a. Identification of disease-causing organisms in storage and in the field
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between common storage and field disease-causing organisms.

subtopics.content: b. Diseases caused by fungi, bacteria, nematodes and viruses; symptoms, damage, transmission and control
subtopics.objective: Relate disease-causing organisms to damage, symptoms and modes of spread; apply appropriate control methods.

subtopics.content: c. Side effects of preventive and control methods, e.g. pollution, poisoning and disruption of ecosystems
subtopics.objective: Relate each control method to its side effects.

subtopics.content: a. Pests of agricultural plants in the field and in storage; types, importance, and principles and methods of prevention and control
subtopics.objective: Identify field and storage pests, assess their economic importance, and relate prevention and control methods to different pests.

subtopics.content: b. Life cycles of biting insects, e.g. grasshopper; boring insects, e.g. weevils; sucking insects, e.g. aphids and cotton strainer
subtopics.objective: Describe insect life cycles and apply this knowledge to pest prevention and control.

subtopics.content: c. Common pesticides and their side effects
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between common pesticides and examine their modes of action on pests.

subtopics.content: a. Importance of forests as sources of wood, pulp, fibre and other forest products
subtopics.objective: Relate various forest products to their uses.

subtopics.content: b. Conservation: regulation, exploitation, regeneration, afforestation, agroforestry and management systems such as taungya, alley and ley
subtopics.objective: Compare different forest conservation methods and apply them appropriately.

topics.title: Forms and Classification of Major Farm Animals in West Africa

subtopics.content: a. Species, breeds, distribution and uses
subtopics.objective: Classify various breeds of farm animals and identify where they are found.

subtopics.content: b. External features of cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, rabbits and poultry
subtopics.objective: Identify the uses of different species of farm animals and their characteristic features.

subtopics.content: Common terms used in animal husbandry, e.g. calving, kidding, castrate, tupping, veal and mutton
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between the various terms used in animal husbandry.

topics.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals

subtopics.content: a. Functions of tissues and organs of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between the functions of various tissues and organs of farm animals.

subtopics.content: b. Animal body systems: digestive systems in ruminants and non-ruminants, reproductive, respiratory, urinary (excretory) and nervous systems
subtopics.objective: Compare different body systems in farm animals.

subtopics.content: c. Effects of environmental changes on physiological development, e.g. climate change, temperature, relative humidity and light
subtopics.objective: Determine the effects of climate change and other environmental changes on farm animals.

subtopics.content: a. Gametogenesis, oestrus cycle, signs and periods of heat, secondary sexual characteristics, gestation periods, parturition and hormones in reproduction
subtopics.objective: Explain reproduction in farm animals and determine the role of hormones in reproduction.

subtopics.content: b. Development, nourishment and birth of the young; mammary glands and lactation
subtopics.objective: Trace development in farm animals from fertilization to birth and care of the young.

subtopics.content: c. Egg formation, incubation and hatching in poultry
subtopics.objective: Trace the process of egg formation and incubation in poultry.

subtopics.content: a. Feed nutrients and their functions
subtopics.objective: Identify the various feed nutrients, their sources and functions.

subtopics.content: b. Feeds and feeding: simple ration formulation, balanced ration, pasture and forage crops such as guinea grass, elephant grass, giant star grass, Andropogon species and Calopogonium species; hay and silage preparation; maintenance and production rations
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between types of animal feeds and their formulation; relate types of rations to different classes of livestock.

subtopics.content: c. Nutrient deficiencies: causes and symptoms of malnutrition and their correction in farm animals
subtopics.objective: Trace symptoms to nutrient deficiencies in farm animals and apply appropriate corrective measures.

subtopics.content: Housing, feeding, sanitation and veterinary care of ruminants, pigs, rabbits and poultry under intensive, semi-intensive and extensive systems, from birth to slaughter
subtopics.objective: Apply different management practices for farm animals.

subtopics.content: a. Animal diseases (pathology): environmental predisposing factors, causal organisms, symptoms, transmission and effects; prevention and treatment of diseases caused by viruses, bacteria, fungi and protozoa
subtopics.objective: Identify farm-animal diseases and causal agents; classify diseases by symptoms and transmission; apply appropriate preventive and curative measures.

subtopics.content: b. Parasites (parasitology): life cycles and economic importance of endoparasites, ectoparasites and disease vectors; prevention and control by dipping, spraying, deworming and sanitation
subtopics.objective: Classify livestock parasites, determine their role in disease transmission, trace parasite life cycles from egg to adult, and apply appropriate prevention and control methods.

subtopics.content: a. Fish culture systems and common fish, e.g. tilapia and catfish; extensive systems including inland and deep-sea fishing, lakes and rivers; semi-intensive systems such as dams; intensive systems such as fish ponds; pond establishment and management including fertilization, liming and desilting
subtopics.objective: Identify common fish in West Africa; differentiate fish-farming systems; determine factors to consider in intensive fish farming.

subtopics.content: b. Fish harvesting and processing: drag nets, hook and line, curing, sun-drying, smoking and fishery regulations
subtopics.objective: Assess advantages and disadvantages of fish harvesting and processing methods; determine appropriate catching and preservation methods; identify fishery regulations in Nigeria.

subtopics.content: c. Wildlife management: habitat conservation, feeding, domestication, harvesting, processing and wildlife regulations
subtopics.objective: Identify animals found in West African game reserves, give reasons for establishing game reserves, and identify common wildlife regulations.

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance of apiculture
subtopics.objective: Relate bee-keeping to economic development.

subtopics.content: b. Types of bees, e.g. exotic and indigenous bees
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between various types of bees.

subtopics.content: c. Methods of bee-keeping, e.g. traditional and modern bee-keeping
subtopics.objective: Classify methods of bee-keeping.

subtopics.content: d. Equipment and safety measures in bee-keeping
subtopics.objective: Identify bee-keeping equipment, their uses and necessary precautionary measures.

sections.sectionTitle: Section D: Agricultural Economics and Extension

subtopics.content: a. Land: types of land ownership in West Africa
subtopics.objective: Understand the meaning and uses of land, identify forms of land ownership, examine their effects on agriculture, and differentiate land features and their effects on land use.

subtopics.content: b. Labour
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between types and sources of labour and their effects on agricultural production.

subtopics.content: c. Capital
subtopics.objective: Compare sources of capital and associated problems.

subtopics.content: d. Management
subtopics.objective: Determine the functions of a farm manager in an agricultural enterprise.

subtopics.content: a. Demand and supply
subtopics.objective: Relate demand to supply in agricultural production and interpret graphical representations of demand and supply.

subtopics.content: b. Production function: input/input, output/output and input/output relationships; stages of production, diminishing returns, scale of preference and choice
subtopics.objective: Relate input to output and deduce economic concepts from graphical representations.

subtopics.content: c. Characteristics of agricultural production: small farm holdings, biological limits, climate susceptibility, seasonality and price elasticity of demand and supply
subtopics.objective: Distinguish common features of agricultural production and produce; compute elasticity of demand and supply.

subtopics.content: a. Labour relations, including supervision
subtopics.objective: Identify ways of achieving labour efficiency.

subtopics.content: b. Types of labour, including permanent labour
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between types and sources of labour.

subtopics.content: c. National labour laws and regulations
subtopics.objective: Apply national labour laws and regulations.

subtopics.content: a. Qualities, functions and problems of a farm manager
subtopics.objective: Identify the qualities, functions and problems of a farm manager.

subtopics.content: b. Records and record-keeping: types and importance, including livestock records and profit-and-loss account books
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between types of farm records and give reasons for keeping farm records.

subtopics.content: c. Stock evaluation: gross and net profits; appreciation, depreciation and salvage value
subtopics.objective: Determine gross and net margins, appreciation, depreciation and salvage value.

subtopics.content: d. Agricultural insurance: meaning, importance, types and problems
subtopics.objective: Examine the relevance of agricultural insurance, determine appropriate insurance schemes and identify associated problems.

subtopics.content: e. Agricultural financing: meaning, importance, types and problems
subtopics.objective: Identify the relevance of agricultural finance and determine problems associated with agricultural finance.

subtopics.content: a. Importance of marketing
subtopics.objective: Evaluate the importance of agricultural marketing.

subtopics.content: b. Marketing channels
subtopics.objective: Classify marketing agents and their functions; determine how marketing channels can pose problems for agricultural production.

subtopics.content: c. Characteristics of agricultural products affecting their marketing
subtopics.objective: Determine the characteristics of agricultural products that affect their marketing.

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance
subtopics.objective: Identify the importance of agricultural extension.

subtopics.content: b. Roles of Agricultural Development Programmes, universities, research institutes and farmers' organizations (cooperative societies)
subtopics.objective: Analyse the roles of government and non-governmental organizations in agricultural extension education.

subtopics.content: c. Extension methods, including demonstration plots, visual aids and mass media
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between the various extension methods.

subtopics.content: d. Problems of agricultural extension in West Africa and possible solutions
subtopics.objective: Examine problems of agricultural extension in West Africa and provide possible solutions.

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance
subtopics.objective: Examine the relevance of farm surveying to agriculture.

subtopics.content: b. Common surveying equipment, their uses and care
subtopics.objective: Classify common surveying equipment and explain their uses and care.

subtopics.content: c. Common survey methods
subtopics.objective: Differentiate between common survey methods.

subtopics.content: d. Principles of farmstead planning
subtopics.objective: Apply survey principles to farmstead layout and identify factors to consider in farmstead planning.

subtopics.content: Identification, use and maintenance of simple farm tools
subtopics.objective: Identify, use and maintain simple farm tools, and compare their advantages and disadvantages.

subtopics.content: a. Types: machinery, e.g. tractor and milking machine; implements
subtopics.objective: Identify common farm machinery and implements and classify machinery according to their uses.

subtopics.content: b. Uses and maintenance of farm machinery and implements
subtopics.objective: Operate farm machines and implements and apply appropriate maintenance routines.

topics.title: Mechanization and Sources of Farm Power

subtopics.content: a. Sources of farm power, e.g. animals and machines
subtopics.objective: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of various sources of farm power and their applications.

subtopics.content: b. Advantages and disadvantages of agricultural mechanization
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between the advantages and disadvantages of mechanization.

subtopics.content: c. Problems and prospects of mechanized agriculture in West Africa
subtopics.objective: Assess the problems and prospects of mechanized agriculture in West Africa.

subtopics.content: a. Traditional and modern methods of food processing, e.g. gari, rice and groundnut processing
subtopics.objective: Identify the importance of agricultural processing and differentiate between methods of processing agricultural produce.

subtopics.content: b. Storage
subtopics.objective: Identify and compare different storage methods and apply appropriate storage methods to different crops.

subtopics.content: Basic terms, e.g. tissue culture, anther culture, in vitro fertilization and genetic engineering
subtopics.objective: Use basic terms in biotechnology and explain the importance and applications of biotechnology.

subtopics.content: a. Features of computers
subtopics.objective: Identify the various components of a computer.

subtopics.content: b. Uses of computers in agriculture: disease and weather forecasting, ration formulation, databases and simulation studies
subtopics.objective: Use computers to enhance agricultural practices.

subtopics.content: c. Communication gadgets, e.g. mobile phones and the internet
subtopics.objective: Use communication gadgets to improve agricultural production.

topics.title: Introduction to Agricultural Research and Statistics

subtopics.content: a. Basic concepts in planning agricultural experiments, e.g. hypothesis, treatment and control
subtopics.objective: Use basic concepts in agricultural experiments.

subtopics.content: b. Interpretation of results, e.g. measures of central tendency and experimental errors
subtopics.objective: Draw inferences from experimental results and compute simple measures of central tendency.
